questions.q: A domain keeps 90 days of application logs. Only the last 7 days are searched often; older logs are queried rarely but must stay searchable, and are never updated. How should the team cut storage cost with the least manual work?

options.t: Add more hot data nodes with larger EBS volumes
options.why: Wrong: it keeps all data on the most expensive tier.

options.t: An ISM policy that moves indexes to UltraWarm after 7 days, then deletes them
options.why: Right: UltraWarm keeps read-only data in S3 at lower cost and ISM automates the move and delete.

options.t: Move old indexes to cold storage and query them there
options.why: Wrong: cold indexes are not searchable until migrated back to warm.

options.t: Set replicas to 0 on every index
options.why: Wrong: it risks data loss and does not shrink storage much compared with a tier change.

questions.explain: Rarely searched, read-only, still searchable: UltraWarm via ISM.
questions.remember: Old immutable data that must stay searchable → UltraWarm, automated with an ISM policy (hot → warm → cold → delete).
variants: Data rarely read and does not need to be searchable → cold storage.
Data must be updated again → migrate it back to hot.
Ad-hoc SQL on archived logs, very cheap → S3 plus Athena.

questions.q: A production domain needs 99.99% availability and fast recovery from an Availability Zone failure without data redistribution. Which configuration meets this?

options.t: Multi-AZ without Standby across 2 AZs with 2 data nodes
options.why: Wrong: this option offers 99.9% and can mean downtime on an AZ loss.

options.t: Multi-AZ with Standby: 3 AZs, 3 dedicated masters, data nodes in multiples of 3, at least 2 replicas
options.why: Right: the standby AZ activates in under a minute and no data has to move.

options.t: A single-AZ domain with 5 dedicated masters
options.why: Wrong: masters do not give AZ resilience and 5 only adds cost.

options.t: A domain with automated snapshots only
options.why: Wrong: snapshots are for recovery, not availability.

questions.explain: Multi-AZ with Standby is the 99.99% layout.
questions.remember: 99.99% availability on a domain → Multi-AZ with Standby (3 AZs, 3 masters, 3n data nodes, 2+ replicas, Auto-Tune).
variants: 99.9% is enough or an existing workflow needs it → Multi-AZ without Standby.
Standby needs a Region with 3 AZs.
Backups and recovery, not availability → snapshots.

questions.q: A team asks for 2 dedicated master nodes for a production domain to save money. What should you recommend?

options.t: Use 2 masters, since one is a standby
options.why: Wrong: 2 masters have no quorum after one fails.

options.t: Use 1 master
options.why: Wrong: one dedicated master is prohibited.

options.t: Use 3 dedicated masters
options.why: Right: 3 gives a quorum of 2 and is the recommended production count.

options.t: Use 4 masters for extra safety
options.why: Wrong: 4 is no better than 3 and can hurt Multi-AZ.

questions.remember: Dedicated masters: always 3 for production (quorum 2), never an even number; 5 works but wastes money.
variants: Lose quorum → reads and writes fail.
Masters are spread across 3 AZs even if data nodes use 2.
More shards or nodes → bigger master instance type.

questions.q: A domain turns red. Which statement is correct and what is the most urgent concern?

options.t: Red means some replicas are unassigned; it is harmless
options.why: Wrong: that is yellow.

options.t: At least one primary shard is unassigned; automated snapshots fail and ISM does not run while red
options.why: Right: act fast, as unfixed red for about two weeks can lose data permanently.

options.t: All shards are assigned but latency is high
options.why: Wrong: that is not a health color meaning.

options.t: The cluster is read-only but healthy and snapshots continue
options.why: Wrong: snapshots fail while red.

questions.explain: Red = primary unassigned; snapshots and ISM stop.
questions.remember: Red → primary shard unassigned, snapshots fail, ISM stops, data loss after about two weeks. Yellow → only replicas unassigned.
variants: One-node domain with 1 replica → yellow, expected.
Fix path → restore from the automated snapshot, add capacity, or reindex.
Alarm on ClusterStatus.red ≥ 1.

questions.q: A company needs semantic search for a RAG application over millions of embeddings with hybrid keyword and vector queries. Load is spiky and the team wants no capacity planning. What fits best?

options.t: An OpenSearch Serverless vector search collection
options.why: Right: OCUs scale automatically and the vector collection type supports k-NN plus keyword search.

options.t: An OpenSearch Serverless search collection
options.why: Wrong: search collections do not support k-NN indexes.

options.t: MemoryDB for Redis OSS
options.why: Wrong: it is fast but memory-bound, and not the best fit for large-scale hybrid keyword and vector search.

options.t: A time series collection
options.why: Wrong: it is for logs and metrics, not vectors.

questions.explain: Vector collection type for k-NN on Serverless.
questions.remember: Spiky GenAI vector workload with no ops → OpenSearch Serverless vector search collection. The collection type cannot be changed later.
variants: Relational data plus vectors → Aurora PostgreSQL pgvector.
Ultra-low latency in-memory vectors → MemoryDB.
Vectors with graph traversal → Neptune Analytics.

questions.q: A k-NN workload uses HNSW and queries slow down after the vector set grows. `KNNGraphMemoryUsage` is near the circuit breaker limit. What is the likely cause and fix?

options.t: HNSW graphs exceed off-heap memory; add memory or use quantization or a less memory-hungry method
options.why: Right: graphs are held off-heap and performance drops beyond the budget.

options.t: The refresh interval is too short; raise it
options.why: Wrong: refresh does not affect graph memory.

options.t: Too many dedicated masters; reduce them
options.why: Wrong: masters hold no data or queries.

options.t: Replicas are set to 0; add more
options.why: Wrong: replicas do not reduce graph memory per node.

questions.explain: HNSW is fast but memory heavy.
questions.remember: HNSW = graph, fast, high recall, memory heavy (off-heap, about 25% of RAM by default). IVF needs training and uses less memory.
variants: 32 GiB RAM → about 8 GiB of graphs.
Filters on vectors inside the search → Lucene engine; post-filters can return fewer than k.
Small or filtered sets → exact k-NN.

questions.q: Streaming web logs must reach a domain with no custom code, and any documents that fail to index must be kept. Which service fits?

options.t: Amazon Data Firehose to OpenSearch with failed documents backed up to S3
options.why: Right: it buffers, batches and can back up failed or all documents to S3.

options.t: Lambda polling the logs with a cron job
options.why: Wrong: custom code and polling.

options.t: Athena queries pushed to the domain
options.why: Wrong: Athena queries S3, it does not load data.

options.t: DynamoDB Streams with Lambda
options.why: Wrong: that syncs a DynamoDB table, not web logs.

questions.remember: Streaming logs, no code → Firehose. Parse, enrich or route, or OpenTelemetry traces → OpenSearch Ingestion. Custom logic → Lambda.
variants: Transformation and routing needed → OpenSearch Ingestion (Data Prepper).
Keep a DynamoDB table searchable → Streams + Lambda or zero-ETL.
Query S3 without copying → direct query or Athena.

questions.q: A team must keep a domain's snapshot for one year and move data to another domain. Which approach works?

options.t: Rely on the hourly automated snapshots
options.why: Wrong: they are retained about 14 days and only for cluster recovery.

options.t: Manual snapshots to the team's S3 bucket, using an IAM role trusted by `es.amazonaws.com` and a signed repository registration
options.why: Right: manual snapshots are kept until deleted and can move data between domains.

options.t: Manual snapshots with an S3 Glacier lifecycle rule on the bucket
options.why: Wrong: the snapshot bucket must not use a Glacier lifecycle.

options.t: Multi-AZ with Standby
options.why: Wrong: replicas copy deletes and bad writes, so it is not a backup.

questions.explain: Long retention or migration → manual snapshots.
questions.remember: Automated snapshots: hourly, 336 kept, 14 days, recovery only. Longer retention or moving data → manual snapshots in your S3 bucket.
variants: PassRole error on registration → add iam:PassRole and es:ESHttpPut.
FGAC on → map manage_snapshots to the signing role.
Serverless → manual snapshots are not supported.

questions.q: Analysts must see only some fields and some documents in a domain index, and one sensitive field only as a hash. Which feature provides this?

options.t: An IP-based resource policy
options.why: Wrong: it controls source addresses, not fields.

options.t: Fine-grained access control with document-level and field-level security and field masking
options.why: Right: FGAC adds role-based index, document and field control and masking.

options.t: A security group on the domain
options.why: Wrong: security groups control network access only.

options.t: A deny on `restricted-index/*` in the access policy
options.why: Wrong: it can be bypassed with `_all` or `_bulk`.

questions.remember: Per-index, document or field control or masking on a domain → FGAC (needs HTTPS, encryption at rest, node-to-node encryption; cannot be disabled). Serverless → data access policies.
variants: Aggregations on a masked field → pattern-based masking.
Separate dashboards per team → Dashboards multi-tenancy.
Resource-policy denies are not real isolation.

questions.q: A security team requires a domain reachable only from inside the company VPC. A year later someone proposes switching an existing public domain to VPC. What is the result?

options.t: Switch it in the console with a blue/green change
options.why: Wrong: public and VPC cannot be changed after creation.

options.t: Create a new VPC domain and move data with a snapshot restore or reindex
options.why: Right: network type is fixed at creation.

options.t: Add an IP-based access policy to the VPC domain
options.why: Wrong: IP-based policies are not allowed on VPC domains.

options.t: Enable fine-grained access control to make it private
options.why: Wrong: FGAC is not a network setting.

questions.explain: Public vs VPC is fixed at creation.
questions.remember: Private-only domain → choose VPC at creation; use security groups, not IP policies. Changing later → new domain plus snapshot or reindex.
variants: After creation you can change subnets and security groups but not the VPC.
Reserve 3 × ceil(data nodes ÷ AZs) IPs per subnet.
On-premises access → VPN, Direct Connect or proxy.

questions.q: Writes to a domain start failing with `ClusterBlockException` and `ClusterIndexWritesBlocked` is 1. `FreeStorageSpace` is near zero. What is the best fix?

options.t: Restart the data nodes
options.why: Wrong: it does not free any space.

options.t: Delete old indexes or add larger EBS volumes or instances, and stay under 80% disk
options.why: Right: low free storage blocks writes; free capacity to recover.

options.t: Add more dedicated masters
options.why: Wrong: masters do not store data.

options.t: Increase replicas to 3
options.why: Wrong: replicas consume more storage and worsen it.

questions.remember: Writes blocked or ClusterBlockException → free or add storage. Insufficient storage is the most common cause of instability; size source × (1 + replicas) × 1.45.
variants: Writes rejected with 429 → thread pool full: slow clients and use bulk.
JVMMemoryPressure high → fewer shards or larger instances.
Many tiny shards → shrink or reindex.

questions.q: A domain's encryption key was deleted and `KMSKeyInaccessible` is reported. What is the outcome?

options.t: Re-enable the key to recover the domain
options.why: Wrong: re-enabling fixes a disabled key (KMSKeyError), not a deleted key.

options.t: The domain cannot be recovered; restore data from a manual snapshot into a new domain
options.why: Right: deleted key or revoked grant makes the domain unrecoverable.

options.t: Automated snapshots restore it in place
options.why: Wrong: they are encrypted with the same key and unreadable.

options.t: Switch to an AWS owned key on the existing domain
options.why: Wrong: encryption at rest cannot be changed that way once enabled.

questions.remember: KMSKeyError (disabled) → re-enable the key. KMSKeyInaccessible (deleted or grant revoked) → unrecoverable; use a manual snapshot into a new domain.
variants: Keep the key and its grants safe.
Alarm on AutomatedSnapshotFailure (no snapshot in 36 hours).
Encryption at rest cannot be turned off after enabling.
